lines.japanese: 現場へ着いたのは集合時刻のわずか３分前──
lines.english: I reached the job site with three whole minutes to spare—

lines.japanese: ──にも関わらず俺が一番乗りだったようで、他にはまだ誰もいなかった。あたりに作業員の乗ったワゴンや、資材を運ぶトラックも見当たらない。遅刻したわけでもないのに、なんとなくほっとした。
lines.english: —and somehow I was the first one there. No sign of the vans full of workers or the trucks hauling equipment. I wasn't late, yet I felt oddly relieved.

lines.japanese: 俺は歩道の端のガードレールに尻を預け、スポーツバッグを足元に置いて待ちモードに入った。
lines.english: I leaned my ass against the guardrail at the edge of the sidewalk, set my sports bag at my feet, and entered waiting mode.

lines.japanese: 両手をポケットに突っこんで、自分の白い息を眺める。立ちのぼってゆくそれを目で追いつつ背を反らせば、正面のオフィスビルはすでにほとんどの窓が黒く塗りつぶされていた。
lines.english: Hands buried in my pockets, I watched my breath come out white. I followed it upward, leaning back as it rose. Night had already painted nearly every window in the office building black.
“Hwaaaah...”

lines.japanese: 朝９時に出社して夕方５時に帰るという人種を、宇宙飛行士やプロ野球選手ぐらいの高みに思いながら欠伸した。
lines.english: I yawned and contemplated the species that went to work at nine in the morning and came home at five, beings as exalted as astronauts or professional ballplayers.

lines.japanese: なんで俺はこんな時間から労働に勤しまなきゃならんのかね。それは便利屋の仕事がなかったからです。はっ、なにが便利屋だ、定職につけ定職に。いや、それが出来るなら最初から苦労はしてない。
lines.english: Why did I have to devote myself to honest labor at this hour? Because there hadn't been any handyman work. Hah. Some handyman. Get a steady job, idiot. Of course, if I could do that, I wouldn't be in this mess to begin with.

lines.japanese: いい歳した社会的動物としてどこか軸のぶれた自問自答を展開、ひとしきりグレーな気分になったところで俺は腰を上げた。
lines.english: After this rather off-kilter debate with myself—hardly fitting conduct for a social animal my age—I sank into a suitably gray mood and pushed myself upright.

lines.japanese: 本業──なんだか副業なんだか単なる小遣い稼ぎなんだか我ながら判然としない──のことを思いだして、ガードレールから離れ、ビルの外階段脇を覗きに行った。
lines.english: I remembered my real job—if it was my real job, rather than a side job or merely a way to scrape together pocket money—and left the guardrail to peer beside the building's outdoor stairs.

lines.japanese: 上のフロアへ続くコンクリート階段の下に、数台の自転車が並んでいる。銀が２台に黒が一台、もう一台はババくさい薄緑色。
lines.english: Several bicycles stood beneath the concrete stairs: two silver, one black, and one in a pale old-lady green.

lines.japanese: 俺は一瞥しただけでその場を離れ、隣りのビルとそのまた隣りも調べた。
lines.english: One glance was enough. I moved on to the neighboring building, then the building beyond that.

lines.japanese: だけど、もちろん背もたれ付きの真っ赤なチャリなんてありゃしない。面白くもない結果が得られたあとで、ようやく気付いた。
lines.english: Naturally, there was no bright-red bicycle with a backrest. Only after achieving this thoroughly uninteresting result did I remember:

lines.japanese: そういえばこの辺りは、おとといの夜、やつ自身によってすでに捜索済みだった。お人好しな俺は無駄な運動をしてしまった。
lines.english: she had already searched this neighborhood herself the night before last. Softhearted fool that I was, I had gotten some pointless exercise.

lines.japanese: 「あー、くだんね」
lines.english: “God, what a waste.”

lines.japanese: 屋根付きの自転車置き場から抜けだして歩道に戻ると、中央分離帯寄りの車線に、見覚えのあるワンボックスカーがハザードを点滅させながら減速してきて……停まった。
lines.english: I emerged from the covered bicycle parking and returned to the sidewalk. A familiar minivan slowed in the lane by the median, hazards blinking... and stopped.

lines.japanese: スライドドアが開いて、ぞろぞろと作業着姿の若いのやらおっさんやらが降りてくる。よっこいしょ、俺もスポーツバッグを拾いあげて肩にかけた。
lines.english: The sliding door opened, and workers young and old came piling out. Heave-ho. I picked up my sports bag and slung it over my shoulder.

lines.japanese: さあてメイクマネーでも始めんべえ。
lines.english: All right, then. Time to make some money.

lines.japanese: 「おはよざっす」
lines.english: “Morning.”

lines.japanese: 「おお、えっと……ナリタか、はは、どうした。三日続けて来るなんて、今回はやる気あるじゃねえか」
lines.english: “Oh, uh... Narita, right? Haha. What's gotten into you? Three days running—you're actually motivated this time.”

lines.japanese: 夜勤前のパチンコで確変でも引いてきたのか、ヒゲ監督は機嫌がいいみたいだった。笑うと意外に愛敬がある。家ではいいお父ちゃんなのかもしれない。
lines.english: Maybe he had hit a hot streak at the pachinko parlor before the night shift; the bearded foreman seemed to be in a good mood. His smile was surprisingly charming. Perhaps he was a good father at home.

lines.japanese: 「だからよおオメエ、うち入れって。俺が話進めてやッからさ、な、明日とりあえず履歴書持ってこいよ」
lines.english: “That's why I keep telling you to join our crew. I'll get the ball rolling. Come on—just bring me a résumé tomorrow.”

lines.japanese: 見合い話を勧める親戚のおばちゃんみたいな笑顔。だけど残念ながら、俺には選択肢がない。
lines.english: He smiled like an aunt arranging a marriage. Unfortunately, that option wasn't open to me.

lines.japanese: 「や……すんません。俺、履歴書ないっすから」
lines.english: “Uh... Sorry. I don't have a résumé.”

lines.japanese: 「はは、なに言ってんだぁ。そんなもんコンビニ行きゃ売ってんだろ」
lines.english: “Haha, what are you talking about? They sell blank ones at any convenience store.”

lines.japanese: まいった。そんな親切の押し売りはやめてくれ。仮にも相手は雇用主。いつもみたいに、うるせーほっとけで済ませられないのが困る。
lines.english: This was bad. Spare me the hard sell on kindness. The man was technically my employer; I couldn't dismiss him with my usual *shut up and leave me alone.*

lines.japanese: 「どもっす、まあ、考えとくっす」
lines.english: “Thanks. I'll think about it.”

lines.japanese: 「……あぁ、そうかい」
lines.english: “...Yeah, all right.”

lines.japanese: 俺が迷惑がってると分かったんだろう。満点パパは憮然として、たちまち呆れ顔になった。短いフィーバーだった。
lines.english: He must have realized his offer wasn’t welcome. Model Dad went sullen, then promptly gave me an exasperated look. His hot streak hadn’t lasted long.

lines.japanese: 「なあ」
lines.english: “Hey.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yeah?”

lines.japanese: 「俺んとこの上のせがれもよ、せっかくいい大学出してやったのに、いまじゃ登録制バイトだか何だかで、気が向いたときだけ働いてるご身分だぁ。へっ、若いののあいだじゃ、そういうのが流行ってんのか？」
lines.english: “My oldest boy, see, I put him through a good university, and now he does some kind of agency temp work. Only works when he feels like it. Hah. Is that what's fashionable with young people these days?”

lines.japanese: 「さあ……ひとそれぞれじゃないすか」
lines.english: “Dunno... I think it depends on the person.”

lines.japanese: 俺は頭を下げてその場を離れる。
lines.english: I bowed my head and left.

lines.japanese: 逃げだしたんじゃない。さっさと作業に入るべきだと思ったんだ。
lines.english: I wasn't running away. I had merely decided it was time to get to work.

lines.japanese: 午前２時。
lines.english: Two in the morning.

lines.japanese: あきらかに削岩ドリルのものとは違う、低く吠えるような騒音が、橋脚の向こう、反対車線をまたたく間によぎっていった。
lines.english: A low roar, unmistakably different from a rock drill, swept past in an instant beyond the bridge supports, on the far side of the road.

lines.japanese: スポーツマフラーの排気音。暗いアスファルトを疾走する巨大な弾丸。俺が振りむいたときには、すでにテールランプがはるか彼方に遠ざかり、緩やかなカーブに吸いこまれて消えた。
lines.english: The exhaust note of a performance muffler. An enormous bullet hurtling over black asphalt. By the time I turned, its taillights were already far away, swallowed by a gentle curve.

lines.japanese: しかしあの音は忘れもしない。フレイムなんたらのワンボックスだ。巷でうわさのオオトリカケルは、こんな夜分にどこへお出掛けだろう。俺には関係ない話──
lines.english: But I could never forget that sound. It was the Flame-whatevers' minivan. Where might the notorious Kakeru Otori be venturing at this hour? Nothing to do with me—

lines.japanese: ──でありますように。
lines.english: —or so I prayed.

lines.japanese: しかし俺のひそかな祈りを嘲笑うように、ひとつ先の信号でＵターンしてきたんだろう、消えたはずの排気音がふたたびぐんぐん迫ってきた。
lines.english: As though mocking that private prayer, the vanished exhaust note began swelling toward me again. They must have pulled a U-turn at the next light.

lines.japanese: 「ヤロウ……」
lines.english: “Bastards...”

lines.japanese: 俺はずり下がったヘルメットを親指で直すふりしながら、猛接近する青白い前照灯を睨んだ。
lines.english: Pretending merely to thumb my slipping hard hat back into place, I glared at the bluish-white headlights bearing down on me.

lines.japanese: パールホワイトのワゴンは例によって、封鎖車線のバリケードめがけ高速で直進してくる。ぐんぐん迫るフロントガラスを隔てて、運転席にでかくて丸い禿げ頭が見えた。
lines.english: As usual, the pearl-white van raced straight at the barricade closing the lane. Through the rapidly swelling windshield, I saw a large, round bald head behind the wheel.

lines.japanese: 俺はうなる爆音を浴びながら、ひそやかに眼力を飛ばして祈る。来んな。来んな来んな。来んな来んな来んな。
lines.english: Bathed in the engine's roar, I poured every ounce of force into my glare and prayed in silence. Don't come. Don't come, don't come. Don't come, don't come, don't come.

lines.japanese: 今度は祈りが通じた。ハゲの駆るワゴンは、誘導係のじいさんが逃げだすぐらいの距離まで肉迫したものの、ぎりぎりでステアを切って開放車線へ流れていき、そのままのスピードで俺の真横をすり抜けていった──
lines.english: This time, my prayer was answered. Baldy's van came close enough to send the elderly traffic guide scrambling, but at the last instant it swerved into the open lane and shot past without losing speed—

lines.japanese: ──開けはなった後部席の窓から、皇帝陛下の薄気味悪い微笑みひとつを残して。
lines.english: —leaving behind only His Imperial Majesty's eerie smile, framed in the open rear window.

lines.japanese: 深夜の工事現場を吹きぬけた白い突風。マナーの悪い運転手なんてすでに見飽きてるはずのおっさん達が、あまりの挑発じみたドライビングを目の当たりにして、怒りや呆れに沸きたっていた。気持ちは分かる。
lines.english: A white gale tore through the midnight roadworks. The older men must have seen more than their share of bad drivers, yet even they erupted in anger and disbelief at the sheer provocation of it. I couldn’t blame them.

lines.japanese: 高速道路の下、俺はスコップを杖代わりに立ち、やつらの行方を恨めしく睨んでいた。
lines.english: Beneath the expressway, I stood with my shovel for a cane and glared bitterly after them.

lines.japanese: ヤンキーワゴンはアクセル全開でぐんぐん遠ざかっていくかと思えば──ケツの赤い光がぎらりと輝きを増した──なぜか運転手はブレーキを踏んでいた。
lines.english: The delinquent van appeared ready to race away at full throttle—then the red lights on its ass flared brighter. For some reason, the driver was braking.

lines.japanese: 遠くに見えるワンボックスの後ろ姿が、速度を落としながら歩道ぎわまで左へ寄っていく。
lines.english: Far in the distance, the back of the minivan drifted left toward the curb as it slowed.

lines.japanese: やがて立ちならぶビル十個分ほど遠くで、真珠色の車体は完全に停まった。ちかちかとハザードランプが点滅しはじめる。
lines.english: About ten buildings away, the pearl-colored vehicle finally stopped. Its hazard lights began blinking.

lines.japanese: ……ハザード？
lines.english: ...Hazards?

lines.japanese: え、なんだよ。なに待機状態入ってんだよ。停まるなよ、帰れよ。
lines.english: What the hell? Why are you settling in to wait? Don't stop. Go home.

lines.japanese: しかし今度は祈りが通じなかった。天井の引き戸から複数の頭がひょっこり飛びだして、陽気にぶんぶん手を振りだした。
lines.english: But this time my prayer went unanswered. Several heads popped through the roof hatch and began waving cheerfully.

lines.japanese: 「あいつら……」
lines.english: “Those assholes...”

lines.japanese: 俺は泣きそうになった。
lines.english: I nearly cried.

lines.japanese: 現場に来んなと言ったのはそういう意味じゃねえ……離れて停めればいいなんて意味じゃねえよ……。
lines.english: That wasn't what I meant when I told you not to come to the job site... I didn't mean you could park farther away...

lines.japanese: 「帰れ、もしくは死んでくれ……」
lines.english: “Go home. Or die. Either one...”

lines.japanese: はしゃぎ声とギャハハ笑いの湧きつづけるワゴンを呪いながら睨んでいると、ブレーキランプが力強く５回点滅。いまどき何のサインだろう。
lines.english: I glared at the van and cursed it as shouts and braying laughter continued to bubble from within. Its brake lights flashed five emphatic times. What kind of signal was that supposed to be in this day and age?

lines.japanese: イ・カ・レ・テ・ル……？
なんだ。自分を分かってるじゃないか。
lines.english: Well. At least they understood themselves.

lines.japanese: さー、仕事だ仕事ー。
lines.english: All right. Back to work.

lines.japanese: それから小一時間は経ったと思う。しかしやつらのバンには、一向に発進する素振りが見られなかった。
lines.english: Nearly an hour passed, I think. Their van showed no sign whatsoever of leaving.

lines.japanese: 何度か浮かれた下っ端ロン毛がクルマを降りて、スキップでもしかねない足取りでこちらに近づいてくることはあった。
lines.english: A few times, one of their giddy long-haired underlings climbed out and came toward us with a step just short of skipping.

lines.japanese: それでも遠くから首を伸ばすように様子を伺うだけで、一定以上の間合いに入ってくることはなかった。少しは日本語が理解できるようになったのかもしれない。
lines.english: But he never did more than crane his neck from a distance, never crossing a certain perimeter. Perhaps they had learned to understand a little Japanese.

lines.japanese: 休憩時間に入ると、俺は不本意ながらやつらのクルマに向かっていった。いつまでも待たれていたら、刑事ドラマの犯人役になったみたいで気分が悪い。
lines.english: When break time came, I reluctantly headed for their vehicle. Having them sit there watching me made me feel like the suspect in a police drama.

lines.japanese: それに、ちょっと確認したいことがある。関わるつもりは毛頭ないが、佐久間が最後に言っていたことだけは多少気になっていた。
lines.english: Besides, there was something I wanted to confirm. I had no intention of getting involved, but Sakuma's parting words had been bothering me a little.

lines.japanese: ワゴンへ近付くにつれ、垂れ流しのＢＧＭが聴こえてきた。鳳翔の大好きな、しゃがれ声の絶叫芸術だ。
lines.english: As I approached the van, I began to hear music pouring from it: the hoarse-voiced screaming that Kakeru Otori considered art.

lines.japanese: 「よっ、勤労青年！　精が出るね！」
lines.english: “Yo, working man! Look at you go!”

lines.japanese: 座りっぱなしに飽きたのか、皇帝とその従士は、本皮のシートを離れてアスファルトの上に立っていた。
lines.english: Perhaps tired of sitting, the emperor and his retainer had abandoned the genuine-leather seats and were standing on the asphalt.

lines.japanese: ブラックライトの灯るヤンクな車内では、サブウーハーがダムダム鳴っている。暴力的な重低音がこっちの腹にまでびりびりと響く。
lines.english: Inside the delinquent van, lit by black lights, the subwoofer pounded away. Its violent bass shuddered all the way through my stomach.

lines.japanese: だがそれだけだ。趣味の合わない大ボリュームはしょせん空気を震わせるだけ。俺のハートは震えない──お、いま俺うまいこと言ったぞ。
lines.english: But that was all. Loud music I hated could do no more than shake the air. It would never shake my heart—oh. That was good. I'd just said something clever.

lines.japanese: 「俺のハートは震えない」
lines.english: “My heart remains unshaken.”

lines.japanese: 気に入ったので、目潰しピースに添えて深夜の挨拶とさせていただく。
lines.english: I liked it, so I paired it with a two-fingered eye-jab salute and promoted the combination to my official midnight greeting.

lines.japanese: 「は？　なにそれ？」
lines.english: “Huh? What's that supposed to mean?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、いんだよ。俺のことはいんだよ。おまえら何してんだよ、ひとの職場に来んなっつったろ」
lines.english: “Never mind. I'm not the issue. What the hell are you doing? I told you not to come to my workplace.”

lines.japanese: 「や、なんかねー？　成田が仕事してるとこ超ウケるーって話で、さっきガンガン盛りあがってたらー。急に翔さんが、また見てえなあとか言いだしちゃってー」
lines.english: “Well, see, we were just cracking up over how hilarious you look at work, and then Kakeru suddenly said he wanted to watch it again.”

lines.japanese: 「来る理由にならねえか？」
lines.english: “Is that not reason enough?”

lines.japanese: 「だから、なるわけねーつってんだろ。父親の職場参観に行きたがる小学生か、てめえは。普段はおざなりなデスクワークも今日ばかりはテキパキこなすぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “I keep telling you it isn't. What are you, a grade-school kid begging to visit Daddy at work? ‘Watch Daddy zip through the desk work he usually neglects,’ asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「ぶはァー！　成田っちのツッコミ、今日もナチュラルに冴えわたってるね～！」
lines.english: “Bwahaa! Narita, your comebacks are effortlessly razor-sharp today!”

lines.japanese: ナチュラルじゃない冴え方をしたレゲエ風が、後部席の窓から文字通り会話に首を突っこんできた。その手には、お巡りさんの目に入ったら職質と尿検査まちがい無しの怪しげな手巻き煙草があった。
lines.english: The reggae type, sharp in ways that were anything but natural, literally stuck his head into the conversation through the rear window. One hand held a suspicious roll-up guaranteed to earn him a police stop and urine test if an officer spotted it.

lines.japanese: 「っせえよ、出てくんな。ソレこっち向けんな。服に煙とかニオイとか付いたら、空港で賢いワンちゃんが寄ってきちゃうだろ」
lines.english: “Shut up. Stay in there. Don't point that thing at me. If the smoke or stink gets on my clothes, some clever dog at the airport will come say hello.”

lines.japanese: 俺は若葉の香りがぷんぷんするドレッド頭をむりやり車内に押しもどして、車外のふたりに向きなおった。
lines.english: I forcibly shoved the dreadlocked head, reeking of fresh-cut leaves, back into the van and turned again to the two outside.

lines.japanese: 「いや、そんなことよりアレ。俺おまえらのせいで、今日ひでえ目に遭ってっから。刃物沙汰だからマジで。どーしてくれんの」
lines.english: “More importantly, you assholes got me into serious trouble today. A knife was involved. I mean it. What are you gonna do about that?”

lines.japanese: 「は？　なに、どーしたんだよ。おいおい水くせえなあ、困ったことあんなら正義の味方ＹＦＢに相談しろよ。悪りいようにはしねえからさ」
lines.english: “Huh? What happened? Come on, don't be a stranger. If you're in trouble, talk to the champions of justice at YFB. We won't do you wrong.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、マジかよ。ほんと、頼りになるよなＹＦＢは」
lines.english: “Seriously? I can always count on YFB.”

lines.japanese: 「って違げーよ。だから、困ったことっつーのがそもそもＹＦＢのせいで……うあっ、いま俺ＹＦＢとか言っちゃったよ。ただでさえ自警団とか痛いのに略称だよ。うわ痛てぇー、俺痛てぇー」
lines.english: “No, wait, that’s not it. I’m saying YFB caused the trouble in the first place... Oh God, I just called you YFB. A vigilante gang is pathetic enough, and now I’m using the acronym. Christ, that’s pathetic. I’m pathetic.”

lines.japanese: 「隼人、何が言いたい。おまえの言葉は支離滅裂だ」
lines.english: “Hayato, what are you trying to say? Your words are incoherent.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、ソレおまえにだけは言われたくねーから」
lines.english: “You are the last person I want to hear that from.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、なぁーんだ、成田っちもなんか食ってたの～？　なになに、葉っぱ？　玉～？　紙～？」
lines.english: “Oh, what? Did you take something too, Narita? What was it? Weed? Pills? Blotter?”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえよ。コーラしかキメてねえよ。だからおまえは出てくんなっつの、存在自体が放送コードに引っかかってんだよ」
lines.english: “Shut up. The only thing I’m high on is cola. And I told you to stay in there. Your very existence violates broadcast standards.”

lines.japanese: ふたたび俺は、若葉の香りとそれを誤魔化すために焚いたチャンダン香がぷんぷん漂うドレッド頭を、むりやり車内へ押しもどした。
lines.english: Again, I shoved the dreadlocked head—reeking of fresh leaves and the sandalwood incense burned to disguise them—back into the van.

lines.japanese: 「で、なんだよ、ひでえ目に遭ったって」
lines.english: “So what happened? What was this serious trouble?”

lines.japanese: 「あーあの、アレ、なんつったっけアレ。あいつ、あのホラ無愛想なあいつ、んーっと……」
lines.english: “Uh, the... What was it again? That guy, you know, the unfriendly one. Umm...”

lines.japanese: 俺は頭を下に向けて記憶を探った。プラチナや佐久間たちの口にのぼった、外人みたいな固有名詞……。
lines.english: I lowered my head and rummaged through my memory. That foreign-sounding name Platinum and Sakuma had mentioned...

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうだ、ハリュー・クロード。おまえら、ハリュー・クロードやった？」
lines.english: “Right. Haryu Claude. Did you guys do something to Haryu Claude?”

lines.japanese: 単刀直入に訊いた。遠慮したって意味はない。
lines.english: I asked point-blank. There was no point being coy.

lines.japanese: 鳳は目を剥いて首をひねり、森里は鼻を鳴らして肩を揺らした。
lines.english: Otori's eyes widened as he cocked his head. Morisato snorted, shoulders shaking.

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　おまえ、なに言ってんだ突然……」
lines.english: “Huh? What are you talking about all of a sudden?”

lines.japanese: 「フハハ！　驚いたぞ隼人、よもや貴様の口からカラスの名が挙がるとはなあ。やつに逢ったのか」
lines.english: “Fuhaha! You surprise me, Hayato. I never imagined the Crow's name would pass your lips. Have you met him?”

lines.japanese: 「ひみつ」
lines.english: “Secret.”

lines.japanese: 俺はあくまで中立、どちらの軍にも互いの情報をみだりに伝える気はなかった。
lines.english: I remained strictly neutral. I had no intention of passing either army intelligence about the other.

lines.japanese: 「つか聞いてんのはこっちだよ。どうなの、やったの。ボコにしちゃったのハリュー」
lines.english: “I'm the one asking questions. So? Did you do it? Did you beat Haryu down?”

lines.japanese: 「ハッ！　やってねえよ。いまのところはなァ」
lines.english: “Hah! We haven’t. Not yet.”

lines.japanese: 「マジで」
lines.english: “Seriously?”

lines.japanese: 「ほーう……カラスはいま手負いなのか……くくく」
lines.english: “Hooh... So the Crow is wounded at present... Kukuku.”

lines.japanese: 鳳は歯を覗かせるように、唇を薄く開いた。くそ、失策だ。言ってるそばから情報を与えてしまった。
lines.english: Otori parted his lips just enough to show his teeth. Damn it. A blunder. I had fed him intelligence in the very act of declaring I wouldn't.

lines.japanese: 「便利屋のネットワークか？　耳ざといじゃねえか、成田工務店」
lines.english: “The handyman network, is it? You have sharp ears, Narita Construction.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、ほんと。それ、誰に聞いたん？」
lines.english: “Seriously. Who told you?”

lines.japanese: 「ないしょ」
lines.english: “Classified.”

lines.japanese: 「カラスの信者か」
lines.english: “A believer in the Crow?”

lines.japanese: 正解。だけどピンポンは鳴らしてやらなかった。
lines.english: Correct. But I didn’t ring the bell for him.

lines.japanese: 「えっ！　なになに～。もしかして成田っち、Ｒ－ウィングに加担してんの～！？」
lines.english: “What! What's this? Narita, are you helping R-Wing!?”

lines.japanese: 出てくるなと言ったのに、またレゲエ風がひょっこり首を突っこんできた。
lines.english: Though I had told him to stay inside, the reggae type poked his head out yet again.

lines.japanese: 「マジでー。んじゃおまえ、俺らの敵じゃん」
lines.english: “Seriously? Then you're our enemy.”

lines.japanese: 「ほう！　それも趣深いな！」
lines.english: “Ho! That has a certain charm of its own!”

lines.japanese: 鳳は左頬を向けて俺を見下ろし、猛禽の爪を唇の横に掲げた。
lines.english: Otori looked down at me sidelong, one taloned hand raised beside his mouth.

lines.japanese: 「いいぜアミーゴ、敵だと言うなら久しぶりに遊んでいくかァ……？」
lines.english: “Very well, amigo. If you call yourself our enemy, shall we play for the first time in far too long...?”

lines.japanese: 「ばねーよ。どっち側でもねーっつの。永世中立、一般市民チームだっつの」
lines.english: “Not happening. I told you I'm on neither side. Permanently neutral. Team Ordinary Civilian.”

lines.japanese: どいつもこいつも、ひとをヤンキー扱いしやがってクソが。俺はそんなのとっくに卒業してんだ、おまえらも歳を考えろ。
lines.english: Every last one of them insisted on treating me like a delinquent. Fuck them. I had graduated from that life long ago. They needed to start acting their age.

lines.japanese: 「でも成田っち、ちょっと認識ずれてるヨー」
lines.english: “But Narita, you've got one thing a little wrong.”

lines.japanese: 「あん？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「俺らの敵はＲ－ウィングであってぇ、あーんのガキんちょどもが萌え萌え言っちゃってるカリスマドラマーじゃねーの。だから、うちがハリュー・クロードに手ぇ出す謂われはねーのよ」
lines.english: “Our enemy is R-Wing. It isn't the charismatic drummer all those little brats squeal and go starry-eyed over. We've got no reason to lay a hand on Haryu Claude.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ。いまのところはなァ」
lines.english: “Yeah. For now.”

lines.japanese: 「今ンとこ今ンとこって、いちいち注釈うっせえな。じゃ、いずれはやるつもりなのかよ」
lines.english: “Quit tacking ‘for now’ onto every damn answer. You planning to go after him eventually?”

lines.japanese: 鳳があまりに聞いてほしそうな態だったので、優しくて空気も読める俺は先を促してやった。
lines.english: Otori was so plainly dying for me to ask that I obliged. I was kind like that, and good at reading the room.

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　俺の未来なんて、俺が知るかよ間抜け」
lines.english: “Huh? How the hell should I know my own future, idiot?”

lines.japanese: 「うわ。可愛くねーなあこいつ」
lines.english: “Wow. What an unlovable bastard.”

lines.japanese: 窓枠から突きでたドレッド頭に同意を求める。やつはトロンとした笑顔でんふふふふと喉を鳴らした。
lines.english: I looked to the dreadlocked head protruding from the window for agreement. He gave me a dreamy smile and chuckled deep in his throat.

lines.japanese: 「あんねー、うちの皇帝とハリューは微妙な関係なのよ。水と油っつーか、やー、むしろ火と油？」
lines.english: “See, our emperor and Haryu have a complicated relationship. Like oil and water—or no, more like fire and oil?”

lines.japanese: 「なにそれ。混ぜるな危険？」
lines.english: “What's that supposed to mean? Danger: do not mix?”

lines.japanese: 「そそそ。じゃなかったらアレ、仲良く喧嘩しな系のネコとネズミ」
lines.english: “Right, right. Or maybe they're Tom and Jerry—best friends who never stop fighting.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ……よく分かんねーけど何、要するに仲いいの悪いの、どっち」
lines.english: “Uh... I still don't get it. Are they friends or enemies? Which is it?”

lines.japanese: 「ジャパニーズ、イングリッシュ、ネーデルランズ、ドイチェ……あァ、少なくとも俺の知る言語の中には、俺とやつとの関係を定義する言葉はねえなあ」
lines.english: “Japanese, English, Dutch, German... No. At least among the languages I know, none contains a word capable of defining the relationship between him and me.”

lines.japanese: 「なはは、カッコつけちゃって～。とりあえずケンカ友達ってことでいいんじゃないのお」
lines.english: “Nahaha, listen to you showing off. Can't we just call you two best enemies?”

lines.japanese: 「ハッ！　ヴァガヤローおまえ、凡骨の目にはそう映ってるかもしれねえが、あいにく俺たちはそんな次元に立ってねえんだよ……」
lines.english: “Hah! You imbecile. That may be how it looks to a mediocrity like you, but unfortunately we stand on no such plane...”

lines.japanese: 「やつはよォ、俺と向いてるベクトルが同じなんだよ……ククク、いけ好かねえカラスだが、その点は認めちゃあいるんだぜ……」
lines.english: “His vector points the same way as mine... Kukuku. I cannot stand the Crow, but on that point, I acknowledge him...”

lines.japanese: 「ぶはー！　こここ皇帝が他人を誉めとるばーい！　めめめ珍しーい！」
lines.english: “Bwahaa! Th-th-the emperor just praised another human being! H-how rare!”

lines.japanese: 「はっ……そすね、二人目だ」
lines.english: “Hah... Yeah. That makes two.”

lines.japanese: 森里がどこか含みのある笑いを見せた。皇帝の悪人面がぐらりと円を描くように動き、その血走った目で従順な従士を捕えた。
lines.english: Morisato smiled as though the words carried some private meaning. The emperor’s villainous face swung around in a slow arc until his bloodshot eyes fixed on his obedient retainer.

lines.japanese: 「え。誰、一人目って」
lines.english: “Wait. Who was the first?”

lines.japanese: 俺はまた、このイカれ男の甘酸っぱい初恋話でも引きだせるものかと思って訪ねてみた。
lines.english: I asked, thinking I might draw out another bittersweet little tale of this lunatic's first love.

lines.japanese: 「キャー、もしかしてソレ成田っち～！？」
lines.english: “Eek! Was it Narita!?”

lines.japanese: 「まさか。違げーますよ、ガルーダっすよ」
lines.english: “No way. It was Garuda.”

lines.japanese: 「ガル……なに？　なんだよそりゃ、ゲームの──」
lines.english: “Garu... what? What is that, from a game or—”
“Buh!”

lines.japanese: 突然のことだった。
lines.english: It happened without warning.

lines.japanese: 鳳の長い腕が水平に走ったかと思うや、次の瞬間には森里が歩道に薙ぎたおされて脇腹を押えていた。
lines.english: Otori's long arm swept sideways. An instant later, Morisato lay mown down on the sidewalk, clutching his side.

lines.japanese: 「和馬……余計なことを喋るな……」
lines.english: “Kazuma... Do not speak of things that do not concern you...”

lines.japanese: 「す……すいま、せん……」
lines.english: “S... sorry...”

lines.japanese: 不幸なロン毛はＭ字開脚みたいな情けない姿勢から立ちなおって、のろのろ腰を上げた。ふてくされた表情をしていたが、俺と目が合うと虚勢を張って笑ってみせた。
lines.english: The unfortunate longhair untangled himself from a pathetic, legs-splayed M and slowly hauled himself upright. He looked sulky, but when our eyes met, he put on a swaggering laugh.

lines.japanese: 「あに見てんだよタコ」
lines.english: “Whaddaya looking at, asshole?”

lines.japanese: 「べつに」
lines.english: “Nothing.”

lines.japanese: 俺は優しいから、憐れんでいたとは言わなかった。
lines.english: I was kind, so I didn't tell him I had been pitying him.

lines.japanese: 「でも、成田っちの言ってることが本当なら、ハリュー・クロードは誰にやられたんかねえ？」
lines.english: “But if what Narita said is true, who got to Haryu Claude?”

lines.japanese: 「お、俺はなにも言ってねえよ」
lines.english: “I-I didn't say anything.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、ともかく、もし成田の言ってることがマジなら、Ｒ－ウィング俺らにブチギレなわけっすよね。あいつら空気読めねーから、何してくっか分かんねーすよ、対策練っといた方がよくないすか」
lines.english: “No, but if Narita's telling the truth, R-Wing'll be furious at us, right? Those guys can't read a room, so there's no telling what they'll do. Shouldn't we work out some countermeasures?”

lines.japanese: 「お、俺はなにも言ってねえからなっ」
lines.english: “I-I'm telling you, I didn't say anything!”

lines.japanese: 「しかし仮に隼人の言うことが事実であれば、いささか不愉快ではあるなァ……カラスの信者どもとは永らく遊んで行きたかったんだが、そうも言ってられなくなる……」
lines.english: “Yet if what Hayato says is true, it would be somewhat displeasing... I had hoped to play with the Crow's believers for a long while yet, but we may no longer enjoy that luxury...”

lines.japanese: 「お、俺は何も言ってねッつってんだろお」
lines.english: “I told you, I didn't say anything!”

lines.japanese: 「でー？　そういう成田っちはハリューとどういう関係なのお？」
lines.english: “Sooo, what sort of relationship does *Narita* have with Haryu?”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　いや、俺は無関係」
lines.english: “Huh? None. I've got nothing to do with him.”

lines.japanese: 直接話したことすらねーし。
lines.english: I had never even spoken to him directly.

lines.japanese: 「ま、強いていやあ、おまえらみたいないい歳したアホと違って、善良な一般市民チームってとこだな」
lines.english: “Well, I guess you could call us Team Upstanding Civilian—unlike overgrown idiots like you.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ～っ、善良な一般市民！　あのカラスがあ！？」
lines.english: “What!? Upstanding civilian? The Crow!?”

lines.japanese: 若干イジケ入ってた森里が、いきなりジェットコースターの乗客みたいに万歳して喚声をあげた。
lines.english: Morisato, who had been sinking into a sulk, suddenly flung both hands into the air and shouted like a rider on a roller coaster.

lines.japanese: 「うっひぇー、ありえねー！　ばーか、腹いてーっつうの。あいつがゼンリョーな一般市民だつーなら、なーんで街の治安維持に協力してくんねえんだよ」
lines.english: “No waaay! That’s impossible! Oh, you idiot, my sides are killing me. If he’s such an upstanding citizen, why won’t he help us keep the peace?”

lines.japanese: 「治安維持。なにそれ」
lines.english: “Keep the peace? What are you talking about?”

lines.japanese: 「はん、いいか、よく聞いとけよォ？　あ……」
lines.english: “Hah. Listen close, and I'll tell you. Uh...”

lines.japanese: 忠実な臣下は、偉大なるあるじの顔色をうかがった。
lines.english: The faithful vassal checked the expression of his magnificent lord.

lines.japanese: 「翔さん、針生のこと、こいつに話していいすか」
lines.english: “Kakeru, can I tell him about Haryu?”

lines.japanese: 「クク、隼人……おまえが耳を傾けると言うなら、いつでも俺は、俺の識るすべてを明かしてやるぜえ？」
lines.english: “Kuku. Hayato... If you say you will listen, I am always willing to reveal to you all that I know.”

lines.japanese: 君主は尋ねた臣下ではなく、その隣りの自由人ただ一点を凝視して答えた。粘りつくような気味の悪い視線。こいつはたびたび俺をこういう目で見ていることがある。
lines.english: The sovereign ignored the vassal who had asked and fixed his eyes solely on the free man beside him. An unpleasantly clinging stare. He looked at me this way from time to time.

lines.japanese: 「つか、フツーに喋れフツーに。いちいち一ひねり加えんな」
lines.english: “Just talk normally. Normally. Stop putting a twist on every damn sentence.”

lines.japanese: 俺は屁理屈好きな皇帝陛下の視線から逃れて、体ごとロン毛に振りむいた。
lines.english: I tore myself away from His Argumentative Majesty’s gaze and turned fully toward the longhair.

lines.japanese: 「なに。カラスがなんだって」
lines.english: “So? What about the Crow?”
“Yeah...”

lines.japanese: 森里は一度どこか遠くに視線と息を投げてから、途切れた話を再開した。
lines.english: Morisato let his gaze drift into the distance and breathed out, then picked up where he’d left off.

lines.japanese: 「いや、だって考えてみろって。いくらカラスとＲ－ウィングが直接関係ないったって、少なくともあいつの言葉があのキモい信者たちに影響力あんのは明白だろ。だから俺らは──」
lines.english: “Think about it. Maybe the Crow has no direct connection to R-Wing, but his words obviously influence those creepy believers. So we—”

lines.japanese: 「──つまり正義の味方・柳木原フレイムバーズは、何度も何度もあのお方にお願いしたわけですよ。ハリュー・クロードさん、あなたの鶴の一声で、あの反社会的な非行集団を解散させてくださいって」
lines.english: “—that is, the champions of justice in the Yanagihara Flame Birds—have asked the great man again and again. ‘Mr. Haryu Claude, with one word from you, please disband that antisocial gang of delinquents.’”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん。そしたら」
lines.english: “Huh. And then?”

lines.japanese: 「断わられた。で、まあ、なんのかんのあって、うちの何人かが病院送りにされた」
lines.english: “He refused. Then one thing led to another, and some of our guys got sent to the hospital.”

lines.japanese: なんのかんのってなんだ。省略された言葉はどこに。
lines.english: What the hell was *one thing led to another* supposed to mean? Where had all the words in between gone?

lines.japanese: 「ひでえだろォ？　な、あいつヤバイんだよ、そーゆーやつなんだよ」
lines.english: “Pretty awful, right? I'm telling you, that guy's dangerous. That's who he is.”

lines.japanese: 「つーか、おまえらのお願いの仕方にも問題あったんじゃねえの。メリケンとか釘バットとかチラつかせてお願いしたんじゃねえの」
lines.english: “Sounds like there might've been a problem with the way you asked. Did you ask while waving brass knuckles and nail-studded bats at him?”

lines.japanese: 「え～、どおだったかな～。忘れちったあ、てぃひ」
lines.english: “Hmm, how'd that go again? I forget. Teehee.”

lines.japanese: 「てぃひ」
lines.english: “Teehee.”

lines.japanese: 「てぃひィ！」
lines.english: “Teeheee!”

lines.japanese: やつらは一様に白々しく首をひねった。くだらねー。俺は細く息を吹いた。
lines.english: They all tilted their heads in matching displays of innocence. Stupid. I let out a thin breath.

lines.japanese: 「つーかさ、前にも聞いた気するけど、そもそもおまえら、なんであいつら……あのＲなんたらってチームとケンカしてんの」
lines.english: “I feel like I asked this before, but why are you fighting those guys in the first place? That R-whatever crew.”

lines.japanese: 「んな、説明するまでもないっ！　柳木原フレイムバーズはこの街にはびこる悪を許しません！」
lines.english: “It needs no explanation! The Yanagihara Flame Birds will not tolerate the evil infesting this city!”

lines.japanese: 「いや、建前いいから。やつらの何かが気に入んねーわけだろ。なあ、それなんなの鳳」
lines.english: “Spare me the official line. There's something about them you don't like, right? What is it, Otori?”

lines.japanese: 兵隊の言葉はもういい。俺は将校に回答を求めた。
lines.english: I had heard enough from the foot soldiers. I demanded an answer from the officer.

lines.japanese: 「理由か？　ハハハ！　挙げようと思えばいくらでも挙げられるぜえ？　論理的にも感情的にもォ」
lines.english: “A reason? Hahaha! I could give you as many as you like, both logical and emotional.”

lines.japanese: 「だが、それはやつらも同じだろう。だから衝突する。あらゆる対立構造はそんなもんだ」
lines.english: “But the same is surely true of them. Thus we collide. Every structure of opposition is built the same way.”

lines.japanese: 要するに、お互い“なんとなくムカツク”ってことか。シンプルな行動原理だ。
lines.english: In other words, each side found the other vaguely infuriating. A simple principle of action.

lines.japanese: 昔じいさんが言ってた──力有するもの、なんどきもそれを行使せんと欲する。
lines.english: Grandpa used to say: those who possess power will always wish to exercise it.

lines.japanese: たぶんこいつらは、理由のために力を振るうんじゃなくて、力を振るうために適当な理由を探したんだろう。少年漫画も英雄叙事詩も倒すべき敵がいなきゃ始まらない。
lines.english: These idiots probably hadn't taken up power for the sake of a cause. They had gone looking for a convenient cause so they could exercise their power. Neither boys' comics nor heroic epics could begin without an enemy to defeat.

lines.japanese: 俺は質問を変えた。
lines.english: I changed the question.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、先に手ェ上げたンどっち」
lines.english: “Then who threw the first punch?”

lines.japanese: 「甲に聞けば乙と答える。乙に聞けば甲と答える。ハハハ、なんと意味のない問いだ！　それともおまえは、一方の言葉だけを信じられるほど被催眠性が高いのか？」
lines.english: “Ask Side A and they'll blame Side B. Ask Side B and they'll blame Side A. Hahaha! What a meaningless question! Or are you so susceptible to suggestion that you can accept one side's testimony on its own?”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　御託はいんだよニワトリ、てめさっき、聞かれたことには答えるつったばっかじゃねえか」
lines.english: “Huh? Enough speeches, Chicken. You just said you'd answer whatever I asked.”

lines.japanese: 「なるほど、たしかに言った。あァ、なら答えてやるよ。こいつァ俺とカラスのオーガナイズする、エンターテインメントの品評会だ」
lines.english: “I see. I did indeed say that. Very well, then. This is an entertainment showcase organized by the Crow and me.”

lines.japanese: 「俺もやつも常に飢えている。求めている。探っている。この糞つまんねえ空の下、形こそ違えど、互いに餓えを満たそうと模索している。その成果をひもじい子供たちに与えてやる機会、それこそがこの聖戦の真意だ」
lines.english: “He and I are forever hungry. Seeking. Searching. Beneath this intolerably dull sky, each of us gropes for a way to satisfy that hunger, though our methods differ. This holy war is our opportunity to offer the fruits of those efforts to the starving children.”

lines.japanese: 「あのさ、だからさ、フツーに喋ってくんないフツーに。さっぱり分かんないんだけど」
lines.english: “Listen, I'm begging you. Can you talk normally? Just normally? I have no idea what you're saying.”

lines.japanese: 「あのう、成田っちー。言っとくけど、非はどっちにあんのかとか知りたいんだったら無駄だーよ？　だって、そんなん、どっちにもあんだから」
lines.english: “Um, Narita? If you're trying to work out which side is at fault, don't bother. They're both at fault.”

lines.japanese: 自称“正義の味方”は事も無げにあっさり言いきった。よく分かってる。糞ったれにしちゃ上出来だ。
lines.english: The self-appointed champion of justice said it without batting an eye. He understood the situation surprisingly well. Not bad for a piece of shit.

lines.japanese: 俺はうしろ頭をがしがし掻い……たら、その手が首に巻いていたタオルに触れた。
lines.english: I raked my fingers over the back of my head... and my hand brushed the towel around my neck.

lines.japanese: 「あーそうだ。森里、コレ返すわ」
lines.english: “Oh, right. Morisato, take this back.”

lines.japanese: 俺は森里和馬から贈られたカラータオルを首から引きぬいた。ゆうべはやむを得ず受けとったものの、やっぱなんかこれは違う。いろんな意味で。
lines.english: I pulled from my neck the colored towel Kazuma Morisato had given me. Circumstances had forced me to accept it last night, but something about it still felt wrong. In several senses.

lines.japanese: 「あ？　だから、いらねっての。しかもそんな、おまえが使ったあとのなんて尚更だ、くせーくせー」
lines.english: “Huh? I told you, I don't want it. Especially after you've used it. It stinks, it stinks.”

lines.japanese: やつは鼻筋に皺を刻んで受け取りを拒否した。俺は有無を言わさずヤンキーワゴンの中へ放りなげた。
lines.english: He wrinkled the bridge of his nose and refused to take it. Ignoring his opinion, I tossed it into the delinquent van.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあニワトリ、おまえにやるよアレ。鳥さんにミルキーボムとか落とされたら、大活躍すんぞアレ。あと、いまならぴちぴちイケメンの汗とか染みこんでっから、ブルセラショップで超高値つくかも」
lines.english: “Then it’s yours, Chicken. That thing’ll be a lifesaver if a bird drops a Milky Bomb on you. And right now it’s soaked in the sweat of a fresh young hunk, so you might get a fortune for it at a used-underwear shop.”

lines.japanese: 「ハッ！」
lines.english: “Hah!”

lines.japanese: 鳳は一瞥残して助手席のドアを開けた。
lines.english: Otori left me with one last glance and opened the passenger door.

lines.japanese: 「冷えてきた。和馬、行くぞ」
lines.english: “It’s getting cold. Kazuma, let’s go.”

lines.japanese: 「いーす」
lines.english: “Right.”

lines.japanese: 森里が手をこすりながら後部席のスライドドアへ走る。鳳はナビシートにふんぞり返るとドアを閉めた。新しい窓拭きをダッシュボードにぶちこんでる。意外と律儀なやつだ。
lines.english: Rubbing his hands together, Morisato ran for the sliding rear door. Otori sprawled in the front passenger seat and shut his door, stuffing his new window rag into the glove compartment. Surprisingly conscientious of him.

lines.japanese: ワゴンが発進しようとする間際、俺はふと思いだしたことがあって、ステップに足をかけたところのロンゲに声をかけた。
lines.english: Just as the van was about to pull away, I remembered something and called to the longhair with one foot on the running board.

lines.japanese: 「森里。あんさ、香田に言っといて。あんま今日のことはひとに話すなって」
lines.english: “Morisato. Hey, tell Koda not to say too much to anyone about today.”

lines.japanese: やつはドアにかけた手を止めて、まじまじと俺を見た。
lines.english: His hand froze on the door, and he stared hard at me.

lines.japanese: 「え……ああ、へえ、なに、おまえら今日会ってたんだ？」
lines.english: “Wait... Oh. Huh. You two saw each other today?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、まー、偶然な」
lines.english: “Uh, well, yeah. We just ran into each other.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: ぐあー、がちゃん。
lines.english: Grrr—clunk.

lines.japanese: スライドドアが閉まった。アスファルトの上に立っているのは俺だけになった。
lines.english: The sliding door shut. I was left standing alone on the asphalt.

lines.japanese: 鳳がカーオーディオのボリュームを乱暴に上げた。しゃがれ声の絶叫。俺のハートは震えない。
lines.english: Otori violently cranked up the stereo. Hoarse-throated screaming. My heart remained unshaken.

lines.japanese: 「まー、森里。アレだおまえ、いろいろあるみてーだけど、まあ女と上手くやれよ」
lines.english: “Anyway, Morisato. Sounds like you've got various things going on, but try to make it work with your girl.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 俺の冷やかしに、ロンゲが顔を上げて笑った。運転手はシフトレバーを前に倒した。
lines.english: The longhair raised his head and laughed at my teasing. The driver shoved the gearshift forward.

lines.japanese: 「っせえよ、おまえが言うな。殺すぞ──」
lines.english: “Shut up. You're one to talk. I'll kill y—”

lines.japanese: 言葉をかっさらってワゴンが走りだした。タイヤが鳴くほどの急発進だった。残された排気ガスを避けて、俺は三歩うしろに退く。
lines.english: The van tore away with the rest of his sentence. It launched hard enough to make the tires squeal. I took three steps back from the cloud of exhaust.

lines.japanese: 遠ざかるテールランプ。
lines.english: The taillights receded.

lines.japanese: 「はー、やっと帰ったか……」
lines.english: “Haaah. Finally gone...”

lines.japanese: 戦争ごっこの好きな永遠の子供たちへ──それからここにはいないハリュー・クロードと、さらにはその信者たちへ──俺は二度と来んなの願いを込めて目潰しピースを送る。
lines.english: To those eternal children who loved to play at war—to Haryu Claude, absent though he was, and to all his believers besides—I offered a two-fingered eye-jab salute and a fervent prayer that none of them ever come back.

lines.japanese: 「世界が平和でありますように」
lines.english: “*May peace prevail on Earth.*”
